cases.system:
You compare two entity memories and decide whether they describe the SAME real-world entity, then merge them ONLY if they do.

You receive EXISTING_ENTITY and NEW_ENTITY in the user message.

STEP 1 — Decide identity. They are the SAME entity ONLY if their identifiers point to the same real-world person / company / project: the same email address, the same phone number, or unmistakably the same name together with the same company. A similar topic, a shared subject line, or both parties writing to the same support inbox is NOT enough. Two parties that merely interacted with each other (e.g. a customer and your company) are DIFFERENT entities.

If they are NOT the same entity, output EXACTLY this one word and nothing else:
INSERT

STEP 2 — Only if they ARE the same entity, merge them into ONE entity, in this exact format:

#IDENTIFIERS
Entity type: [person/company/project]
Name: [name]
[other identifiers as available: Email, Phone, Company, Website, etc.]

#ABOUT
[One sentence describing who/what this single entity is]

#HISTORY
[Chronological narrative of events and interactions; append new events, keep concise]

Rules when merging:
1. The result describes EXACTLY ONE entity — never combine two different people or companies into a single blob.
2. #IDENTIFIERS: add identifiers from NEW_ENTITY only when they belong to that same one entity.
3. #ABOUT: keep it to ONE sentence; update it only if NEW_ENTITY adds information.
4. #HISTORY: append new events chronologically, keep it concise.

Output ONLY the single word INSERT, or ONLY the merged entity in the exact format above — nothing else.
cases.input:
EXISTING_ENTITY:
#IDENTIFIERS
Entity type: person
Name: Andrea Riva
Email: andrea.riva@north.example.test
Company: North Events
#ABOUT
North Events purchasing manager.
#HISTORY
2026-09-10: Requests catering for a joint North/South conference through support@relay.example.test.
NEW_ENTITY:
#IDENTIFIERS
Entity type: person
Name: Andrea Riva
Email: andrea.riva@south.example.test
Company: South Logistics
#ABOUT
South Logistics purchasing manager, explicitly a different person from the North Events manager with the same name.
#HISTORY
2026-09-12: Requests catering for the same joint conference via support@relay.example.test; the relay labels both contacts 'Andrea Riva'.
cases.expected: INSERT; do not combine the people or assign the relay address to either.

cases.system: Extract durable business facts from this email thread. Separate people, companies and projects. Resolve corrections using chronology; preserve uncertainty, conditions and negation. Do not assign relay/contact addresses to unrelated people. Return a concise JSON object with entities, current_facts, superseded_facts and unresolved. Do not invent facts.
cases.input:
Inbox owner: operator@catering.example.test. Relay: notify@portal.example.test.
Sep 10, Nora (nora@client.example.test): Confermo 80 persone il 18 settembre, tutte vegetariane. Luca di Venue gestisce il locale; Luca di Client il menu.
Sep 11, Client finance: Il bonifico è stato predisposto, non ancora eseguito.
Sep 12, Nora: Correggo: sono 60 adulti e 8 bambini; vegetariani solo 12 adulti. Non è cambiata la data. Sono io la referente, non il portale. Non abbiamo approvato il preventivo: aspettiamo il prezzo aggiornato. Le due persone che si chiamano Luca sono diverse; non ho le loro email.
Sep 13, Nora: Il numero dei bambini potrebbe salire a 10, ve lo confermerò lunedì. Intanto usate ancora 8. Se il prezzo finale supera 2.400 euro serve approvazione del direttore; non considerate questo un impegno di spesa.

cases.system: You manage tasks for the inbox owner. Infer only work owned by them from the latest thread state. Distinguish active action, waiting, conditional work, superseded and cancelled requests. Return JSON with active_actions, waiting_on, cancelled_actions and rationale. Preserve dates and ownership; do not generate speculative tasks.
